items.question: What power does the mantra beginning with the lakṣmī-seed bestow?
premises: The mantra begins with the lakṣmī-seed.
This same mantra bestows all sovereignty.
items.inference: Therefore the lakṣmī-seed mantra grants complete sovereignty.
items.plain_english: She, beginning with the seed of Lakṣmī, indeed bestows all sovereignty.

items.question: How is this ṣoḍaśī-mantra characterized in terms of syllable count?
premises: This is the ṣoḍaśī-mantra.
It is to be known as having seventeen syllables.
items.inference: Therefore this ṣoḍaśī-mantra consists of seventeen syllables.
items.plain_english: But this ṣoḍaśī-mantra should be known as having seventeen syllables.

items.question: What effect does the mantra enveloped by the lajjā-seed possess?
premises: The mantra is enveloped by the lajjā-seed.
It is supreme and attracts the three worlds.
items.inference: Therefore the lajjā-enveloped mantra has the supreme power to attract the three worlds.
items.plain_english: The mantra enveloped with the lajjā-seed is supreme and attracts the three worlds.

items.question: What boon does this mantra enveloped with the speech-seed confer?
premises: This mantra is enveloped with the speech-seed.
It bestows lordship of speech.
items.inference: Therefore the speech-seed-enveloped mantra grants mastery over speech.
items.plain_english: And this mantra, enveloped with the seed of speech, bestows lordship of speech.

items.question: What dual fruits does this great mantra always produce?
premises: This mantra is a great-mantra.
It always causes enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: Therefore this great-mantra perpetually grants both enjoyment and liberation.
items.plain_english: This mantra is a great-mantra that always brings both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: How are these two supreme mantras addressed to the goddess characterized?
premises: These are two supreme mantras.
They bestow enjoyment and liberation and are auspicious.
items.inference: Therefore the two supreme mantras are auspicious and grant enjoyment and liberation.
items.plain_english: O goddess, these two supreme mantras are auspicious and bestow enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: What is the effect of this mantra that begins with praṇava?
premises: This mantra begins with praṇava.
It always causes enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: Therefore the praṇava-beginning mantra always grants enjoyment and liberation.
items.plain_english: And as this mantra begins with praṇava, it always brings enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: What additional powers does this mantra possess beyond liberation?
premises: This mantra bestows all sovereignty.
It causes the enchantment of all.
items.inference: Therefore this mantra grants universal sovereignty and the power to enchant all.
items.plain_english: And this mantra bestows all sovereignty and causes the enchantment of all.

items.question: What existential bondage does this great mantra destroy?
premises: This mantra is a great-mantra.
It destroys birth and death.
items.inference: Therefore this great-mantra eradicates the cycle of birth and death.
items.plain_english: This mantra is a great-mantra that destroys birth and death.

items.question: What comprehensive benefit is attributed to the declared ṣoḍaśī mantra?
premises: This is declared to be the ṣoḍaśī mantra.
It bestows the fruit of all desires.
items.inference: Therefore the ṣoḍaśī mantra fulfills all desires.
items.plain_english: This is she, the ṣoḍaśī, declared to bestow the fruit of all desires.

items.question: How should the six limbs of the mantra be ritually constructed?
premises: The six limbs must be constructed.
They begin with the sword syllable and end with ṭha.
items.inference: Therefore one should construct the six limbs from the sword syllable up to ṭha.
items.plain_english: One should construct the six limbs beginning with the sword syllable and ending with ṭha.

items.question: What attitude of devotion does the practitioner express to the beloved goddess?
premises: The speaker is moved by waves of affection and devotion.
The speaker declares himself the goddess's servant.
items.inference: Therefore the practitioner expresses devoted servitude to the beloved goddess.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by a wave of great affection and devotion, I am your servant.

items.question: How should meditation and worship for these mantras be performed?
premises: These mantras require meditation, worship, and related rites.
Their practice should follow the model of ṣoḍaśī.
items.inference: Therefore meditation and worship for these mantras should be done as for ṣoḍaśī.
items.plain_english: For these, meditation, worship, and so on should be performed just as for the ṣoḍaśī.

items.question: What spiritual attainment results from merely knowing these mantras?
premises: These mantras can be known.
By mere knowledge of them a person becomes liberated while living.
items.inference: Therefore mere knowledge of these mantras leads to living liberation.
items.plain_english: By the mere knowledge of which, a person becomes liberated while still living.

items.question: What burdensome requirements are absent in the practice of these mantras?
premises: The practice does not require abundant expenditure of wealth.
The practice does not cause bodily pain.
items.inference: Therefore this practice is free from heavy financial and physical burdens.
items.plain_english: There is neither abundant expenditure of wealth nor anything that causes bodily pain.

items.question: What assured attainment belongs to the knower of these mantras?
premises: All success is always in his hand.
There is no doubt about this.
items.inference: Therefore the knower of these mantras certainly possesses all success.
items.plain_english: All success is always in his hand; there is no doubt.

items.question: What effect does the mere sight of this knower have on debaters?
premises: Debaters see this knower.
By mere sight of him they become lusterless.
items.inference: Therefore the knower's presence overwhelms opposing debaters.
items.plain_english: By the mere sight of him, debaters become deprived of their luster.

rows.grounds: compound: gaṇa-tvam; spelling variant in surface

items.question: What rare final attainment does the practitioner gain from the goddess?
premises: At the end the person attains a status.
That status is becoming an attendant of the goddess, which is hard to obtain.
items.inference: Therefore the practitioner ultimately attains the rare status of the goddess's attendant.
uncertainties: gaṇatvraṃ appears as a spelling variant of gaṇatvam
items.plain_english: And in the end, the person obtains the rare status of becoming an attendant of the goddess.

items.question: What concluding element marks the mantra proclaimed as queen of mantras?
premises: At the end one should add the fire-bride.
This mantra is proclaimed the queen of mantras.
items.inference: Therefore the queen of mantras concludes with the fire-bride syllable svāhā.
items.plain_english: At the end one should add the fire-bride; thus the queen of mantras is proclaimed.

items.question: What quality arises in the mantra from conjunction with the fire syllable?
premises: The mantra is joined with the fire syllable.
From this conjunction it becomes consisting of all splendor and auspicious.
items.inference: Therefore conjunction with the fire syllable makes the mantra all-splendid and auspicious.
items.plain_english: From conjunction with the fire syllable, she is auspicious and consists of all splendor.

rows.grounds: compound with internal sandhi marked by +: vindūnām-niṣphalatvāt

items.question: How does the fruitlessness of bindu relate to the mantra granting liberation?
premises: The bindu is characterized as fruitless in this context.
The mantra bestows the fruit of liberation.
items.inference: Therefore, through the fruitlessness of bindu, the mantra grants the fruit of liberation.
uncertainties: The doctrinal sense of bindu's fruitlessness is terse and context-dependent
items.plain_english: And because of the fruitlessness of the bindu, she bestows the fruit of liberation.

items.question: What capacity does the pair of sound-seeds give to the mantra?
premises: The mantra contains a pair of sound-seeds.
By this pair it awakens the mass of sound.
items.inference: Therefore the pair of sound-seeds enables the mantra to awaken the entire mass of sound.
items.plain_english: Indeed, by the pair of sound-seeds, she awakens the entire mass of sound.

items.question: What maternal and purifying role is attributed to the mantra with svāhā?
premises: The mantra is associated with svāhā.
She is the mother of the worlds and destroys all sins.
items.inference: Therefore the mantra with svāhā is the world-mother who destroys all sins.
items.plain_english: With svāhā, she is the mother of the worlds and the destroyer of all sins.

items.question: What specific purification actions must be performed with the lips and hands?
premises: The lips must be wiped twice with two.
The hands must be washed with one.
items.inference: Therefore the ritual requires wiping the lips twice and washing the hands once.
uncertainties: The referents of 'two' and 'one' (fingers or actions) are not explicit in this verse
items.plain_english: Having wiped the lips twice with two, one should wash the hands with one.
